T1.name: Copper trunk
T1.description: Carries voice-frequency signals over bare copper pairs mounted on poles.

T2.name: Loading coil
T2.description: Adds inductance to long copper loops, extending voice range while limiting bandwidth.

T3.name: Phantom circuit
T3.description: Uses transformers to create an additional voice circuit from two physical pairs.

T4.name: Open-wire FDM
T4.description: Multiplexes several telephone channels onto open-wire routes using separate frequency bands.

T5.name: Transcontinental
T5.description: Connects distant regional networks into a coast-to-coast long-distance telephone route.

T6.name: Underground conduit
T6.description: Routes cables through protected underground ducts, reducing weather and accidental damage.

T7.name: Duplex telegraph
T7.description: Allows simultaneous telegraph transmission in both directions over one circuit.

S1.name: Manual switchboard
S1.description: Operators manually connect subscriber lines using plugs, cords, and switchboard jacks.

S2.name: Magneto crank
S2.description: Uses local telephone batteries and a hand-cranked magneto to signal the exchange.

S3.name: Common battery
S3.description: Supplies telephone power centrally from the exchange instead of individual local batteries.

S4.name: Strowger step-by-step
S4.description: Automatically connects calls through electromechanical selectors controlled by dial pulses.

S5.name: Trunk hunting
S5.description: Automatically selects an available trunk from a group of equivalent circuits.

S6.name: Panel switch
S6.description: Uses motor-driven panel banks and senders to automate large urban exchanges.

S7.name: Multi-office trunking
S7.description: Links multiple local exchanges with shared trunks and coordinated interoffice routing.

A1.name: Telephone set
A1.description: Converts speech into electrical variations using a carbon-granule transmitter.

A2.name: Party line
A2.description: Lets several subscribers share one local loop, lowering cost but reducing privacy and capacity.

A3.name: Rotary dial
A3.description: Sends numbered pulse sequences to an automatic exchange by rotating a dial.

A4.name: Wall phone
A4.description: Mounts the telephone set vertically for homes and businesses with limited desk space.

A5.name: PBX
A5.description: Provides private internal extension switching with controlled access to the public network.

A6.name: Bridging bell
A6.description: Connects multiple high-impedance ringers across a line without blocking normal voice current.

A7.name: Lineman test set
A7.description: Portable handset used by technicians to test, monitor, and troubleshoot telephone circuits.

C1.name: Morse telegraph
C1.description: Encodes text as timed electrical dots and dashes for long-distance telegraph communication.

C2.name: Stock ticker
C2.description: Prints continuously updated market prices sent over dedicated telegraph circuits.

C3.name: Telex network
C3.description: Connects teleprinters through a switched international text-communications network.

C4.name: Numbering plan
C4.description: Assigns standardized area codes and telephone numbers for continent-wide automatic routing.

C5.name: Trunk super group
C5.description: Combines frequency-division groups into larger analog carrier hierarchies for high-capacity trunks.

C6.name: Manual toll board
C6.description: Lets operators establish and supervise long-distance calls through dedicated toll positions.

C7.name: Toll cord test
C7.description: Provides centralized testing and fault isolation for long-distance trunks and circuits.

T8.name: L-carrier coaxial
T8.description: Carries hundreds or thousands of analog voice channels over broadband coaxial cable.

T9.name: TD-2 microwave
T9.description: Relays multichannel telephone and television traffic between line-of-sight microwave towers.

T10.name: TAT-1 submarine
T10.description: Provides the first permanent transatlantic telephone service through a submarine coaxial cable.

T11.name: N-carrier FDM
T11.description: Multiplexes multiple analog voice channels over paired copper carrier systems.

T12.name: Troposcatter
T12.description: Sends radio signals beyond the horizon by scattering them through the troposphere.

S8.name: #1 Crossbar
S8.description: Uses crosspoint matrices and electromechanical control to switch local telephone calls.

S9.name: #4 Crossbar toll
S9.description: Applies crossbar switching to high-capacity long-distance and tandem traffic.

S10.name: #5 Crossbar local
S10.description: Provides scalable crossbar switching for large local metropolitan telephone exchanges.

S11.name: DDD
S11.description: Allows subscribers to dial long-distance destinations without assistance from an operator.

A8.name: Touch-tone DTMF
A8.description: Represents dialed digits as pairs of audio frequencies for faster, reliable signaling.

A9.name: Desk phone 500
A9.description: A durable standardized desk telephone widely deployed across the mid-century network.

A10.name: MTS car phone
A10.description: Provides operator-assisted mobile calls through a small number of high-power radio channels.

A11.name: IMTS improved
A11.description: Improves mobile service with automatic dialing, additional channels, and better call handling.

C8.name: SF signaling
C8.description: Uses a single in-band tone to supervise seizure and release of telephone trunks.

C9.name: MF signaling
C9.description: Uses combinations of audio frequencies to transmit routing digits between switching offices.

C10.name: ANI
C10.description: Automatically identifies the originating subscriber number for routing, billing, and services.

C11.name: ONI
C11.description: Records call destination, duration, and timing automatically for billing and traffic analysis.

T15.name: Fiber optic
T15.description: Transmits high-capacity optical signals through low-loss single-mode glass fiber.

T16.name: T1 carrier
T16.description: Digitally carries 24 voice channels at 1.544 Mb/s using time-division multiplexing.

T18.name: SONET
T18.description: Standardizes synchronous optical transport, multiplexing, monitoring, and rapid protection switching.

T19.name: EDFA amplifier
T19.description: Amplifies optical signals directly in fiber without converting them back to electricity.

T20.name: DWDM
T20.description: Carries many optical wavelengths simultaneously through one fiber to multiply capacity.

S15.name: #1ESS electronic
S15.description: Introduces stored-program electronic control to large telephone switching offices.

S16.name: #4ESS digital
S16.description: Digitally switches high-volume long-distance traffic under stored-program control.

S18.name: #5ESS modular
S18.description: Provides modular digital switching for local, tandem, and service-provider applications.

A15.name: ISDN BRI
A15.description: Delivers two digital bearer channels and one signaling channel over a subscriber line.

A17.name: 1G AMPS
A17.description: Provides first-generation analog cellular voice service with automatic handoff between cells.

A18.name: 2G GSM
A18.description: Provides second-generation digital cellular voice, messaging, authentication, and international roaming.

A20.name: 2.5G GPRS
A20.description: Adds packet-switched mobile data services to existing second-generation GSM networks.

A21.name: ADSL
A21.description: Uses higher frequencies on copper loops to provide asymmetric broadband alongside telephone service.

C15.name: SS7
C15.description: Separates signaling from voice paths for fast call setup, routing, roaming, and services.

C16.name: IN
C16.description: Carries packet data through reliable virtual circuits across public data networks.

C17.name: TCP/IP
C17.description: Interconnects heterogeneous packet networks using a common addressing and transport protocol suite.

C20.name: DNS
C20.description: Translates human-readable domain names into network addresses through a distributed hierarchy.

C24.name: BGP
C24.description: Exchanges reachability information between independently administered networks on the global Internet.

T22.name: 40G DWDM
T22.description: Raises optical backbone capacity using 40-gigabit channels over dense wavelength multiplexing.

T23.name: 100G coherent
T23.description: Uses coherent detection and digital signal processing for 100-gigabit optical channels.

T26.name: GPON
T26.description: Shares passive fiber from an optical line terminal among multiple broadband subscribers.

S22.name: MPLS
S22.description: Forwards packets through short labels, enabling traffic engineering and service separation.

S23.name: Softswitch
S23.description: Moves call-control logic into software while media gateways connect legacy and packet networks.

S27.name: LTE EPC
S27.description: Provides LTE mobility, authentication, session control, and gateways to external packet networks.

A22.name: 3G UMTS
A22.description: Introduces third-generation wideband cellular radio for improved voice and mobile data.

A23.name: 3.5G HSPA+
A23.description: Enhances UMTS with faster packet scheduling, modulation, and radio-link techniques.

A24.name: FTTH
A24.description: Runs optical fiber directly to customer premises for high-capacity fixed broadband.

A25.name: 4G LTE
A25.description: Provides all-IP fourth-generation mobile broadband with wide channels and low radio latency.

C19.name: ATM
C19.description: Transports voice, video, and data in fixed-size cells with service-quality controls.

C25.name: IP/MPLS
C25.description: Combines IP routing and MPLS traffic engineering into a scalable carrier backbone.

C26.name: IMS
C26.description: Provides standardized IP-based control for voice, messaging, multimedia, and converged services.

C28.name: NFV
C28.description: Runs network functions as software workloads instead of dedicated proprietary appliances.

T29.name: 1.6T coherent
T29.description: Uses advanced coherent modulation and digital processing to carry 1.6-terabit optical wavelengths.

T31.name: Hollow-core fiber
T31.description: Tests air-guiding fiber designs intended to reduce propagation delay and nonlinear effects.

S29.name: SDN
S29.description: Separates network control from forwarding so carrier infrastructure can be programmed centrally.

S30.name: Network Slicing
S30.description: Creates isolated logical networks with distinct performance and service policies on shared 5G infrastructure.

A29.name: 5G NR
A29.description: Introduces flexible fifth-generation radio numerologies, massive MIMO, and broader spectrum support.

A30.name: 5G mmWave
A30.description: Uses millimeter-wave spectrum for extreme capacity over short, obstruction-sensitive coverage areas.

A32.name: LEO satellite
A32.description: Provides broadband through large fleets of low-orbit satellites with frequent handoffs.

C29.name: MEC
C29.description: Places computing and service processing near users to reduce latency and backbone traffic.

C31.name: 5GC SBA
C31.description: Uses cloud-native service-based functions to manage 5G sessions, mobility, policy, and authentication.

C33.name: AI RIC
C33.description: Optimizes open radio-access networks through near-real-time control applications and telemetry.
